title: Crown Roast of Pork From Serious Eats
description:
Ask your butcher for your crown roast at least a day or two in advance to make sure they can order it and prepare it. Aim for around 1 1/2 chops per person, or 2 chops per person if you want leftovers. Other aromatics like minced garlic or chopped herbs can be added along with the salt and pepper if desired. To prevent ends of ribs from burning, cap each with a piece of aluminum foil if desired.
Fast twitch muscle, like pork loin in the Crown Roast, has no connective tissue to break down. As soon as it reaches its final temperature, it's done. Holding it at that temperature for extended periods of time will change it very little, except to dry it out. Cook it to temperatures of 125°F in the case of beef, 145°F for chicken, 110°F for tuna, or 140°F for pork.
ingredients: One 6- to 10-pound crown roast of pork (12 to 20 chops, 1-2 per person)
Some thyme, sage, garlic, salt, freshly ground black pepper, and olive oil
directions: Preheat oven to 250°F and adjust oven rack to center position.
Blend the spices together for a nice generous rub, then season pork roast liberally with the mixture.
Place on a wire rack set in a rimmed baking sheet, transfer to oven, and roast until internal temperature reaches 135°F, about 2 hours.
Remove from oven and tent with foil for at least 15 minutes and up to 45 minutes.
Meanwhile, increase oven temperature to 500°F. Return roast to oven and cook until crisp and browned on the exterior, about 10 minutes.
Remove from oven, tent with foil, allow to rest for 15 minutes, then carve by slicing in between each rib and serve, maybe with a simple parsley-caper sauce.
